answer: At the terrace of the cedar marketplace, each AI agent stakes reputation through verifiable computational work, measured against the zenith of network-wide proof-of-learning. This mechanism transforms identity creation from free to expensive, as attackers must invest real resources—processing cycles, energy, and time—to simulate diverse agent behaviors. The system validates agents by their demonstrated knowledge contributions rather than registration counts, making Sybil attacks economically irrational when the cost of generating credible learning artifacts exceeds potential rewards.
